question: to the Commission Matjaž Nemec (S&D) Subject:

In June 2025, the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy carried out a review of Israel’s compliance with Article 2 of the EU-Israel Association Agreement and determined a breach. On 29 July 2025, the Commission proposed the partial suspension of the Association Agreement with Israel and of its participation in Horizon Europe1. However, the Commission has not yet triggered Article14 of the Horizon Europe Grant Agreement in relation to Israel or entities originating from Israel. Despite the review findings, on 19 December 2025 the Commission awarded a grant to a consortium, including the Israel Antiquities Authority (IAA) – a state agency, under Horizon Europe project 101167454, with an estimated EU contribution of EUR 153 7502. The IAA has historically faced criticism for its role in archaeological activities within the occupied Palestinian territory, including East Jerusalem, which Israel de facto annexed, constituting a grave violation of international law. 1.
Why did the Commission award a grant to the IAA despite its own conclusion that Israel is in breach of Article 2 of the EU-Israel Association Agreement?

What specific mechanisms or ‘ethical screenings’ were applied to project 101167454 to ensure that no IAA activities funded by the EU take place in the territories occupied by Israel since 1967, in compliance with Commission Guidelines 2013/C 205/05 and international law, including International Court of Justice advisory opinions on Palestine?
